title: Can you use static methods in an interface, how are they called, and are they inherited by implementing classes?
shortTitle: How are static methods in interfaces called?

s1_definition.profdef: Yes, interfaces can have `static` methods since Java 8. They are called ONLY via `InterfaceName.method()` — never via an implementing class or instance. They are NOT inherited: if `AccountService` has `static BigDecimal calculateInterest(...)`, you CANNOT call `SavingsAccountServiceImpl.calculateInterest(...)` — you MUST call `AccountService.calculateInterest(...)`. They CANNOT be overridden. They replace the old "companion utility class" pattern: instead of `Collections.sort()` (utility class) + `Collection` (interface), Java 8 puts `Comparator.comparing()`, `Predicate.not()`, `List.of()`, `Map.of()` directly ON the interface. This keeps related functionality together.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of the RBI (Reserve Bank) publishing a standard interest calculator on their website (interface static method). Every bank in India can USE the RBI calculator by visiting rbi.gov.in/calculator (InterfaceName.method()). But no bank can put that calculator on their OWN website and claim it as theirs (not inherited). HDFC cannot say "HDFC.calculateInterest()" — it must say "RBI.calculateInterest()". The calculator belongs to RBI (the interface), not to any specific bank (implementing class).
s1_definition.oneliner: Interface static methods: called via InterfaceName.method() ONLY. NOT inherited. NOT overridden. Replaces companion utility classes. Keeps related logic with the interface.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Yes, interfaces can have `static` methods since Java 8. They are called ONLY via `InterfaceName.method()` — never via an implementing class or instance. They are NOT inherited: if `AccountService` has `static BigDecimal calculateInterest(...)`, you CANNOT call `SavingsAccountServiceImpl.calculateInterest(...)` — you MUST call `AccountService.calculateInterest(...)`. They CANNOT be overridden. They replace the old "companion utility class" pattern: instead of `Collections.sort()` (utility class) + `Collection` (interface), Java 8 puts `Comparator.comparing()`, `Predicate.not()`, `List.of()`, `Map.of()` directly ON the interface. This keeps related functionality together.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Think of the RBI (Reserve Bank) publishing a standard interest calculator on their website (interface static method). Every bank in India can USE the RBI calculator by visiting rbi.gov.in/calculator (InterfaceName.method()). But no bank can put that calculator on their OWN website and claim it as theirs (not inherited). HDFC cannot say "HDFC.calculateInterest()" — it must say "RBI.calculateInterest()". The calculator belongs to RBI (the interface), not to any specific bank (implementing class).

**One line to remember:** Interface static methods: called via InterfaceName.method() ONLY. NOT inherited. NOT overridden. Replaces companion utility classes. Keeps related logic with the interface.

sections.s3_banking:
**Problem — The bank has a `TransactionService` interface implemented by NEFT, IMPS, UPI, and RTGS services.** Common utility logic (tax calculation, reference number generation, amount validation) was in a separate `TransactionUtils` class. This creates a maintenance problem: related logic is split across two files. The team moves all utility methods as `static` methods on the `TransactionService` interface itself, keeping everything in one place.

**What the project will show:** Static factory methods, static utility methods, proof that static methods are NOT inherited, NOT overridden, and the "before/after" comparison of utility class elimination.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** NEFT transfer request arrives. Controller delegates to NeftTransactionService.

**Step 2.** NeftTransactionService needs a transaction ID. It calls `TransactionService.generateTxnId("NEFT")` — NOT `this.generateTxnId()` or `NeftTransactionService.generateTxnId()`. The static method belongs to the INTERFACE.

**Step 3.** Static method generates "NEFT-20240115-000001" using date + atomic counter.

**Step 4.** `TransactionService.isValidAmount(50000)` validates: not null, >= 1, <= 10M → true.

**Step 5.** `TransactionService.calculateGST(50000)` computes: service charge Rs.5.90 (>10K) × 18% = Rs.1.06.

**Step 6.** Response returned: amount Rs.50,000 + GST Rs.1.06 = total debit Rs.50,001.06.

**Step 7.** ImpsTransactionService does the same but with "IMPS" prefix and "COMPLETED" status (instant).
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ STATIC vs DEFAULT — KEY DIFFERENCE ═══

  interface TransactionService {
      TransferResponse transfer(req);         // ABSTRACT — impls override

      default void log(String msg) { ... }    // DEFAULT — inherited, overridable
      static String generateTxnId(ch) { ... } // STATIC — NOT inherited, NOT overridable
  }

  NeftTransactionService implements TransactionService:
    ├─ transfer()      → (Recommended) OVERRIDES abstract method
    ├─ log()           → (Recommended) INHERITED from default (can override)
    └─ generateTxnId() → (Avoid) NOT INHERITED! Must call TransactionService.generateTxnId()

  ═══ CALLING PATTERNS ═══

  TransactionService.generateTxnId("NEFT")       → (Recommended) InterfaceName.method()
  NeftTransactionService.generateTxnId("NEFT")   → (Avoid) COMPILE ERROR!
  neftInstance.generateTxnId("NEFT")              → (Avoid) COMPILE ERROR!

  ═══ BEFORE vs AFTER: UTILITY CLASS ELIMINATION ═══

  BEFORE Java 8 (two files):
    interface Collection<E> { ... }
    class Collections {                       ← separate utility class
        static void sort(List list) { }
        static List unmodifiable(List l) { }
    }

  AFTER Java 8 (one file):
    interface List<E> extends Collection<E> {
        static <E> List<E> of(E... e) { }     ← static ON the interface!
        static <E> List<E> copyOf(Coll c) { } ← everything in one place!
    }

  ═══ COMMON USE CASES ═══

  Factory:    List.of(), Map.of(), TransactionService.quickTransfer()
  Utility:    Comparator.comparing(), Predicate.not(), calculateGST()
  Validation: TransactionService.isValidAmount(), isValidIFSC()
  Generator:  TransactionService.generateTxnId()
```
sections.s5c_hld:
**What is HLD?** The bird's-eye view. Here static interface methods act as factory/validation helpers co-located with the interface they serve, replacing scattered utility classes across the banking platform.

```
  ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
     HLD — Payment Platform using Static Interface Factory Methods
  ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  ┌─────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
  │ Net Banking │  │ Partner API  │  │ Batch Loader │  ← Client Layer
  └──────┬──────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘
         └────────────────┼─────────────────┘ HTTPS
                          ▼
                ┌──────────────────────┐
                │    API Gateway       │  ← JWT, routing
                └──────────┬───────────┘
                           ▼
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
         │  PaymentService (×4)                      │  ← Application Layer
         │  uses PaymentMethod.of(type)   (static)   │  factory on interface
         │  uses Money.valid(amount)      (static)   │  validator on interface
         │  (static methods NOT inherited by impls)  │
         └──────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                JDBC │
                     ▼
         ┌──────────────────┐
         │ PostgreSQL       │  ← accounts, payments
         └──────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Redis: payment-method config cache               │
  │  Observability: Prometheus, ELK, Jaeger           │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The HLD insight: instead of a sprawling PaymentUtils utility class sitting apart from the PaymentMethod type, the static factory `PaymentMethod.of(type)` and validators live ON the interface itself. The whole platform calls one obvious namespace, and the helpers travel with the contract they belong to.
sections.s5d_lld:
**What is LLD?** Zoom into the interface and its implementations to show that static methods belong to the interface type, are called as InterfaceName.method(), and are NOT inherited by implementing classes.

```
  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
       LLD — Static Methods in Interfaces (FAANG Level)
  ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  ┌─ Design Patterns Used ────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Factory Method (static): PaymentMethod.of(type) → impl           │
  │     WHY: centralize creation on the interface, hide concretes     │
  │  Static Utility co-location: replaces separate *Utils classes     │
  │     WHY: helper lives with the type, better cohesion              │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ SOLID Principles Applied ────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  S: interface owns its own factory/validation helpers             │
  │  O: new payment type = new impl + one case in of(), callers same  │
  │  D: PaymentService depends on PaymentMethod, not concretes        │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ── Class Diagram ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │        <<interface>> PaymentMethod           │
  │  ──────────────────────────────────────────── │
  │  + pay(amount: BigDecimal): Receipt          │  abstract (inherited)
  │  + static of(type): PaymentMethod            │  NOT inherited
  │  + static supportedTypes(): List<String>     │  NOT inherited
  └───────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                  │ implements  (static methods do NOT pass down)
      ┌───────────┼────────────────┐
      ▼           ▼                ▼
  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────────┐
  │ UpiPay   │ │ NeftPay  │ │ CardPay      │
  │+pay()    │ │+pay()    │ │+pay()        │
  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────────┘
    (UpiPay.of(...) is a COMPILE ERROR — call PaymentMethod.of)

  ── Call Chain (Main Scenario) ─────────────────────────────

  1. PaymentService.send("UPI", Rs.50,000, Rajesh SAV2001)
  2.   → PaymentMethod m = PaymentMethod.of("UPI")   static factory
  3.       (resolves to new UpiPay() internally)
  4.   → Receipt r = m.pay(new BigDecimal("50000"))   instance method
  5.   → return r
  6.  Note: m.of(...) and UpiPay.of(...) are NOT valid — static
  7.        methods are called only via the interface name.
```

The LLD makes the rule explicit: a static method defined on an interface is scoped to that interface and must be invoked as `PaymentMethod.of(...)`. Implementing classes like UpiPay do NOT inherit it, so `UpiPay.of(...)` does not compile. This is exactly why static interface methods are the modern replacement for utility classes — the helper stays bound to the type it serves.
sections.s6_takeaway:
Interface static methods were added in Java 8 to allow utility logic to live on the interface itself instead of in a separate companion utility class. They are called exclusively via `InterfaceName.method()` and are NOT inherited by implementing classes — `NeftTransactionService.generateTxnId()` does not compile; you must call `TransactionService.generateTxnId()`. They cannot be overridden. This is fundamentally different from default methods, which are inherited and can be overridden by implementing classes.

In my transaction gateway service, the TransactionService interface has one abstract method (transfer) and four static methods: generateTxnId for reference number generation, calculateGST for tax computation, isValidAmount for validation, and quickTransfer as a factory that returns a lambda implementation. All four are called via `TransactionService.methodName()` by both NeftTransactionService and ImpsTransactionService. Before Java 8, these would have been in a separate `TransactionUtils` class — now everything is in one place, making the code easier to navigate and maintain.

The practical impact is seen across the Java standard library: `List.of()`, `Map.of()`, `Set.of()` replace `Collections.unmodifiableList()`. `Comparator.comparing()` and `Comparator.naturalOrder()` replace manual Comparator instantiation. `Predicate.not()` replaces verbose negation lambdas. The pattern is: if a utility method is conceptually tied to an interface, make it a static method on that interface rather than creating a separate utility class.
